properties.areaDesc: Coconino, AZ; Navajo, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 2:50AM MST until October 24 at 3:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Woodruff to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until 300 AM MST /400 AM MDT/ Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring. Further rises in the water levels are expected. Deadly
flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 243 AM MST /343 AM MDT/, river gauges along the Little
Colorado River at Woodruff, Holbrook, and Winslow reported
significant rises and elevated flow. Stages at both Holbrook and
Winslow are expected to reach action stage later this morning.
- For the Little Colorado River near Woodruff:
At 2:30am MST /3:30am MDT/ the stage was 14.72 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 15.28 feet is expected at 3:00am MST /4:00am
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 20.5 feet: Bankfull. Portions of residential yards flooded.

- For the Little Colorado River at Holbrook:
At 2:30am MST /3:30am MDT/ the stage was 14.22 feet.
Flood Stage is 15.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 16.41 feet is expected at 1:00pm MST /2:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 15.5 feet: Railroad bridge affected. Overflow on South Bank.

- For Little Colorado at Joseph City:
At 2:30am MST /3:30am MDT/ the stage was 5.93 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 6.5 feet is expected at 2:00pm MST /3:00pm
MDT/ Friday.
Impacts:
At 7.5 feet: Potential downstream lowland overflow.

- For the Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 2:00am MST /3:00am MDT/ the stage was 17.04 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest of 17.23 feet is expected at 10:00am MST
/11:00am MDT/ Saturday.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Leupp, Birdsprings, Homolovi Ruins State Park, and Clear Creek
Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued October 23 at 4:44AM CDT until October 23 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM NOON TODAY TO 8 PM MDT
THIS EVENING DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR SLOPE AND
BOWMAN COUNTIES...

.Very warm and breezy conditions are expected across southwest North
Dakota this afternoon into early this evening. In far southwest North
Dakota, afternoon relative humidities are expected to drop to 15 to
20 percent, with winds around 20 mph and gusts to 40 mph. Therefore a
Red Flag Warning has been issued for Bowman and Slope counties in far
southwest North Dakota.

* AFFECTED AREA...Slope and Bowman.

* TIMING...From noon today to 8 PM MDT this evening.

* WINDS...South winds around 20 mph with gusts to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity 15 to 25 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity and warm temperatures can contribute to extreme
fire behavior.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 3:37AM MDT until October 23 at 5:45AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by thunderstorms and excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Grand County in east central Utah...
Northeastern San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 545 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 337 AM MDT, Emergency management reported heavy rain in the
warned area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes, but is not limited to, the following streamsand
drainages...
Florida River, Spring Creek, Ute Creek, Salt Creek and Dry Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Low-lying areas along McElmo Creek between Cortez and Aneth.
- Flooding is ongoing at Bartlett Wash and Hunters Canyon.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 545 AM MDT EARLY THIS MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Northern Bristol Bay Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 23 at 1:34AM AKDT until October 24 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels most likely around 1.0 to 2.0 feet above
the normal highest tide line, with highest water levels
expected near Togiak.

* WHERE...Northern Bristol Bay Coast.

* WHEN...10 AM Friday to 7AM Saturday

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Bering front arrives to the Southwest
Alaska coast Friday morning, bringing a prolonged period of
strong southerly winds towards the coast. These winds will
result in elevated water levels and high surf. This period of
winds will coincide with two tidal cycles and push water
levels 1.0 to 2.0 feet above the normal highest tide line.
Water levels are expected to quickly drop off Saturday morning
as winds decrease, alleviating coastal concerns.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM THIS MORNING TO 7 AM AKDT SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 1:34AM AKDT until October 24 at 1:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal flooding, with water levels of 2.0 to 3.0 feet
above the normal highest tide line, and 35 to 50 mph winds
with gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...8 AM Friday through 1 AM Saturday, particularly around
high tides near 10 AM and 10 PM Friday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely scenario is for water
levels to be 2.0 to 3.0 ft above the normal high tide line.
While unlikely, the worst case scenario for Kipnuk is for
water levels to be 3.5 to 4.0 feet above the normal high tide
line, while the worst case for Kwigillingok is 4.0 to 5.0 feet
above the normal high tide line. The 10 PM Friday peak, with
the aforementioned high tide, is expected to be the higher of
the two peaks. We are closely monitoring this storm. In the
meantime, please have a plan in place.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 8 AM THIS MORNING TO 1 AM AKDT SATURDAY

properties.areaDesc: Aleutians East Borough
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 23 at 1:33AM AKDT until October 23 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 35 to 50 mph with gusts up to 75 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Aleutians East Borough.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds are expected to steadily increase out of
the south-southeast mid morning on Friday and are on track to peak
in intensity early Friday afternoon with gusts expected to reach 75
mph. Wind gusts begin to decrease Friday evening, and dramatically
drop off by early Saturday morning with the frontal passage.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must drive.

NWSheadline: HIGH WIND WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM AKDT THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island; Interior Kuskokwim Delta; Western Capes; Northern Bristol Bay Coast
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued October 23 at 1:33AM AKDT until October 24 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 35 to 50 mph with gusts up to 75
mph.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta, Western Capes, and Northern Bristol Bay
Coast.

* WHEN...From 7 AM this morning to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The strongest winds are expected to start by 1
PM AKDT Friday for the Kuskokwim Delta, Northern Bristol Bay,
Platinum, and Goodnews Bay. For the Western Capes, the strongest
winds are expected near Cape Newenham, with winds for Platinum and
Goodnews Bay expected to be near 60 mph. For Northern Bristol Bay,
the strongest winds are expected near Togiak, while gusts up to 50
mph are expected for Dillingham. Winds are expected to steadily
diminish through Saturday as the front moves inland and weakens.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must drive.

NWSheadline: HIGH WIND WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 7 AM THIS MORNING TO 4 AM AKDT SATURDAY
